title: Fan charts and pullback of arbitrary saturated fan blowup towers
statement:
For an fs log scheme $(X,M)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], a strict morphism is a log morphism whose source log structure is the log structure pulled back from its target. On a Zariski log scheme, meaning a log structure associated to one on the Zariski site, a fan chart $c:(X,\overline M)\to(F,\mathcal P_F)$ is a morphism of sharp monoidal spaces inducing an isomorphism $c^{-1}\mathcal P_F\simeq\overline M$, where $F$ is a fine fan [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].

(i) Every fs log scheme admits strict etale neighborhoods carrying such a fan chart. If $X$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and all characteristic group completions are torsion free, a finite family of quasi-compact strict etale neighborhoods covers $X$, each with a chart to a saturated torsion-free affine fan; quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover.

(ii) Given any fan chart $c$ of an fs log scheme $(V,N)$ and any finite saturated blowup tower $F_\bullet\to F$, there exists a tower $c^*F_\bullet$ of saturated log blowups of $(V,N)$. At a stage with center $J\subset\mathcal P_{F_i}$ its log center is the inverse image in $N_i$ of the ideal generated by $c_i^{-1}J$ in $\overline N_i$. There are fan charts $c_i:(V_i,\overline N_i)\to(F_i,\mathcal P_{F_i})$ at every level. In particular $\overline N_{i,\bar v}\simeq\mathcal P_{F_i,c_i(\bar v)}$. Nonempty coherent centers pull back to nonempty coherent log ideals. These constructions are compatible with composition of fan blowup towers and with strict base change of log schemes; the latter is taken in the fs category.
